rule: A level is recommended for a role only if it meets that role's floor on two consecutive runs AND its p95 latency fits the role's cadence. Defaults stay 'default' whatever the numbers (overview rule 9). Floors are never retuned.

reconciliation.scope: Notes only. rule, roles[*].floor, roles[*].latency, levels and reasoningBudget are unchanged (a floor is never retuned). Arm expectations are restated against the code as built on master 7e9f3ab8; they are not floors.
reconciliation.replyEffortIsNotTheRolePath: The 2026-10-02 reply effort (runtime/replyEffort*, five llama.cpp TC keys / CC thinking_budget_tokens, medium = 400) applies only to LOUD main-reply generations. Every R3 role call goes through the Connection Manager: TC CM calls never fire GENERATE_AFTER_DATA and CC CM calls are typed quiet (custom-request.js:601), so no role ever receives those keys. R3 measures the role mapping, src/services/stHost/reasoningPayload.ts, unchanged except DeepSeek: TC = unsupported ('Text Completion sends a raw prompt'), custom = enable_thinking only (collapsed), deepseek = off/low/high with medium collapsed into high (mapped 2026-10-02 on v26-measure-prep, 05 F8).

arms.artemis-tc: Expectation STANDS as declared. The five llama.cpp budget keys exist server-side (15-model-config.md section 'Reasoning effort A/B', b11046) and the reply overlay sends them, but reasoningPayload still refuses TC for roles. So: default x2 full + one level (off) on one case per role to prove the refusal (report reasoning.unsupported set, request unchanged). Note the arm profile 'Artemis RunPod RP' uses the 'Gemma 4 Thinking' instruct, so its default already thinks, uncapped; read's answer budget is 512 tokens and may read reasoning-exhausted at default. Teaching the role mapping the five keys is a product change (proposed, not built); if it is built before the run, this arm becomes a full sweep and this note must be rewritten BEFORE the first call.
arms.artemis-cc: F5 is now answered (15-model-config.md: chat_template_kwargs.thinking_budget_tokens caps CC reasoning on b11046; reasoning_effort low/high are byte-identical; no kwarg = thinking on). The role mapping does NOT send thinking_budget_tokens (customPlan sends enable_thinking only), so the declared collapse STANDS for the code as built. 'Collapsed' is the thinking switch only: R2 still adds reasoningBudget[level] (512/2048/6144) to max_tokens, so low/medium/high differ in max_tokens and therefore in exhaustion. Minimum run = default, off, medium (the 'on' arm) x2; low and high are optional extra cells that measure exhaustion only. If customPlan gains thinking_budget_tokens before the run, the arm becomes a full sweep; rewrite this note first.
arms.deepseek: Profile 'deepseek 4.1 flash' (id 975bc0dc-956b-4cd8-9fe4-9be158e01847, source deepseek, model deepseek-flash, read from lane 5 settings.json 2026-10-02). Mapping as built (reasoningPayload.ts deepseekPlan, 05 F8): ST's sendDeepSeekRequest (chat-completions.js:1122-1124, 1137) sends thinking {type: enabled|disabled} from include_reasoning and forwards reasoning_effort only with include_reasoning; DeepSeek's API (api-docs.deepseek.com/api/create-chat-completion) takes none/low/high/max, default high, and maps medium to high. So off is a real 'no thinking' arm, low and high are distinct efforts, and medium is the same request as high except max_tokens (+2048 vs +6144); its role row says 'has no medium level: it runs as high'. Minimum run = default, off, low, high x2 full; medium x2 is optional (exhaustion only, like artemis-cc low/high). Note: 'default' sends no effort and lets the profile/preset decide; DeepSeek's own default is thinking enabled at high. Hosted calls cost money: meter with the session spend tooling.
